intent.raw_query: New Zealand South Island, $4000, hiking and bungee jumping, November 2026

experiences.name: Tongariro Alpine Crossing
experiences.description: One of New Zealand's most iconic day hikes, crossing volcanic terrain with stunning views of emerald lakes and craters. Book an early shuttle from Queenstown or Wanaka to maximize daylight hours on the trail. Stay in Taupo or National Park Village the night before to avoid wasting time on Day 1 with a late arrival.
experiences.location: Tongariro National Park, Central North Island

experiences.name: Nevis Bungy Jump
experiences.description: New Zealand's highest bungy jump at 134 meters, operated by AJ Hackett in a gondola suspended above the Nevis River. A bucket-list adrenaline experience near Queenstown. Book in advance to secure your preferred time slot and combine with nearby accommodation in Queenstown central to avoid long transfers.

experiences.name: Routeburn Track Day Hike
experiences.description: A world-class multi-day track accessible as a rewarding day hike from the Routeburn Shelter trailhead. Offers dramatic alpine scenery, beech forests, and mountain views. Stay in Glenorchy village (45 min from Queenstown) the night before to get an early start and make the most of the trail without rushing.

experiences.name: Kawarau Bridge Bungy
experiences.description: The world's first commercial bungy jump site at 43 meters above the Kawarau River, operated by AJ Hackett. A historic and thrilling experience with a scenic river backdrop. Located just 23 km from Queenstown central, making it easy to combine with central accommodation and other Queenstown activities on the same day.

experiences.name: Hooker Valley Track to Mueller Glacier
experiences.description: A relatively easy but breathtaking 10 km return hike through Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park, crossing swing bridges with direct views of New Zealand's highest peak and glacial lakes. Stay in Mount Cook Village (within the park) to eliminate long morning drives and enjoy the trail at golden hour with fewer crowds.
experiences.location: Mount Cook Village, Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - New Zealand South Island
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

Stay in Mount Cook Village (within the park) to eliminate long morning drives and enjoy the trail at golden hour with fewer crowds.
experiences.location: Mount Cook Village, Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Queenstown Airport at 13:00. Collect luggage and take the Orbus public bus (Route 1, ~$4 NZD) to Queenstown town centre. Check in to Queenstown Boutique Stay, freshen up, and take a leisurely walk along the Queenstown waterfront and Steamer Wharf to get your bearings. Enjoy views of Lake Wakatipu and The Remarkables mountain range.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Queenstown town centre and explore the lively pedestrian mall. Head to Fergburger (world-famous budget-friendly burger joint) for a hearty dinner to recover from the flight.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight or airport snack
meals.lunch: Grab a meat pie or sandwich from a supermarket (New World or Countdown) near the airport or town centre (~$5 NZD)
meals.dinner: Fergburger on Shotover Street - iconic, filling burgers from ~$15 NZD

day_by_day.notes: Pick up a Queenstown i-SITE map from the visitor centre near the waterfront. Buy a local SIM card at the airport (Skinny Mobile is budget-friendly). Stock up on groceries at New World supermarket for snacks and breakfasts to save money throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning hike up Queenstown Hill Time Walk (Te Tapu-nui). The trailhead starts at the top of Belfast Street, just a short walk from town. The 2-3 hour return hike offers panoramic 360-degree views of Lake Wakatipu, the Remarkables, and Cecil Peak. Free to access.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to town and head to the Queenstown Gardens for a relaxing walk through the rose gardens and along the lake edge. Visit the free Kiwi Birdlife Park entrance area or explore the lakefront. Consider renting a bike from Around the Basin (~$20-30 NZD/half day) and cycling the Queenstown Trail along the lake.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset over Lake Wakatipu from the waterfront. Head to the Night Markets (Monday nights on the Queenstown waterfront, seasonal) for cheap, diverse street food options from $5-12 NZD per dish.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation - muesli, yogurt, or toast from supermarket groceries (~$3-5 NZD)
meals.lunch: Pak'nSave or New World supermarket deli - grab a sandwich or sushi rolls (~$6-8 NZD)
meals.dinner: Queenstown Night Market street food stalls - try local vendors for $10-15 NZD total

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy shoes for the Queenstown Hill hike. Bring water and sunscreen. The hike gains about 500m in elevation so start early to avoid midday heat in November. Check if Night Markets are running on arrival as schedules can vary.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Shotover Jet or research budget options for the morning. Alternatively, hike the Ben Lomond Track lower section to the Saddle (4-5 hours return, free). Start from the Gondola base or take the Gondola up ($32 NZD) to save time. The trail through beech forest offers stunning alpine scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: BUNGEE JUMPING EXPERIENCE: Book the Kawarau Bridge Bungy with AJ Hackett - the world's first commercial bungee jump site, 43m above the Kawarau River (~$205 NZD). Watch others jump for free if budget is tight, or consider the Ledge Bungy in town (~$205 NZD) which is slightly more accessible. Book in advance online for best pricing.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate your bungee jump! Head to the Pub on Wharf or Minus 5 Ice Bar for one drink. Dinner at a budget-friendly spot in town to relax and recount the day's adventure.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered - oats or toast at accommodation (~$3 NZD)
meals.lunch: Pack a homemade sandwich and snacks from supermarket to eat at Kawarau Bridge (~$5 NZD)
meals.dinner: Vudu Cafe & Larder or Devil Burger on the mall - burgers or wraps from ~$14-18 NZD

day_by_day.notes: Bungee jumping is a major budget splurge day. Book AJ Hackett online in advance for potential discounts. Check weight requirements (min 35kg, max 230kg). The Kawarau Bridge site includes a free viewing platform so friends can watch. Videos and photos cost extra (~$50 NZD) - decide in advance if worth it.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Glenorchy (45 min drive from Queenstown). Take the Ritchies bus or join a budget shuttle (~$20-30 NZD return). Walk the free Glenorchy Lagoon Walkway (1.5 hours, flat and easy) through wetlands with views of snow-capped peaks - a stunning Lord of the Rings filming location.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Glenorchy area with the Diamond Lake and Rocky Mountain Loop Track (2-3 hours return, free). Alternatively, walk to Paradise - a nearby area with incredible mountain and river scenery. Picnic lunch by the Dart River.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown by late afternoon. Relax at the accommodation. Cook a simple pasta or stir-fry dinner using supermarket ingredients to save budget for bigger experiences ahead.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation (~$3-5 NZD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from supermarket - sandwiches, fruit, snacks eaten at Glenorchy (~$8-10 NZD)
meals.dinner: Self-catered at accommodation - pasta with pesto and veggies (~$5-7 NZD)

day_by_day.notes: Glenorchy is one of the most scenic drives in New Zealand - the road along Lake Wakatipu is breathtaking. If driving, fuel up in Queenstown as there's no petrol station in Glenorchy. November weather can be unpredictable in the mountains so bring a rain jacket. Check bus schedules in advance as services are limited.

day_by_day.morning: ROUTEBURN TRACK DAY HIKE: Depart Queenstown early (7:00am) via shuttle to the Routeburn Shelter trailhead (~$55-65 NZD return with Tracknet or similar). Begin hiking the Routeburn Track from the Routeburn Shelter end. The first section through beech forest to the Routeburn Falls Hut (2-3 hours one way) is spectacular.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue hiking beyond the Falls Hut to Routeburn Falls and the alpine basin above if energy and time allow (additional 1-2 hours). Enjoy panoramic views of the Humboldt Mountains and surrounding wilderness. This is a world-class track so take your time and soak in the scenery. Begin return hike by 2:00pm to catch the shuttle back.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown tired but exhilarated. Soak tired legs with a warm shower. Dinner at a local pub or takeaway. Early night to recover.

meals.breakfast: Early self-catered breakfast at accommodation - porridge or toast by 6:30am (~$3 NZD)
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch - sandwiches, energy bars, nuts, and fruit eaten at Routeburn Falls (~$8-10 NZD)
meals.dinner: Winnies Gourmet Pizza on The Mall - budget pizzas from ~$20 NZD (share a large one to save)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Tracknet shuttle in advance as they fill up quickly in November (peak season). The Routeburn Track is a Great Walk so the trail is well-maintained and clearly marked. Wear proper hiking boots, carry 2L of water, sunscreen, and a warm layer as alpine conditions can change rapidly. Total hiking distance for the day hike to Falls Hut and back is approximately 16km.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning after the Routeburn hike. Sleep in and enjoy a slow breakfast. Walk the easy Frankton Track along the lake edge (free, 3km one way) for gentle exercise without straining tired muscles. Visit the Queenstown i-SITE to plan the Wanaka and Mount Cook legs of the journey.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the free Queenstown Arts Centre or browse the local shops along the mall. Head to the Queenstown waterfront for a swim if weather permits (Lake Wakatipu is cold but refreshing in November). Alternatively, visit the free Queenstown Museum in the Eichardt's area to learn about local gold rush history.
day_by_day.evening: Happy hour drinks at a local bar (many Queenstown bars have 5-7pm specials). Dinner at the Queenstown Night Market if running, or grab affordable Thai or Indian takeaway from one of the many cheap eateries on Shotover Street.

meals.breakfast: Treat yourself to a cafe breakfast - try Vudu Cafe for eggs on toast (~$14-18 NZD) as a reward after the big hike
meals.lunch: Supermarket deli or food court at Queenstown Central (~$8-10 NZD)
meals.dinner: Thai or Indian takeaway on Shotover Street - curry and rice from ~$14-16 NZD

day_by_day.notes: Use this rest day to do laundry if needed (laundromats near town centre), charge all devices, and prepare gear for the upcoming Wanaka and Mount Cook sections. Book any remaining activities in advance. Check road conditions and weather forecasts for the next few days.

day_by_day.morning: Pack up and check out of Queenstown Boutique Stay. Take the InterCity bus or Naked Bus to Wanaka (~$15-25 NZD, 1.5 hours via Crown Range Road - the highest sealed road in NZ). Arrive in Wanaka by late morning. Check in to a budget hostel (Wanaka Backpacker or Base Wanaka, ~$30-40 NZD/night dorm).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the famous Wanaka Tree (That Wanaka Tree) on the lake shore - free and iconic photo opportunity. Continue along the Wanaka lakefront walkway (free, 2km) with stunning views of Lake Wanaka and Mt Aspiring National Park peaks. Hire a paddleboard or kayak from Paddle Wanaka (~$25-30 NZD/hour) for a lake experience.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Wanaka town centre - much more relaxed and cheaper than Queenstown. Watch the sunset over Lake Wanaka from the lakefront - one of the most beautiful sunsets in New Zealand. Dinner at a local eatery in town.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at Queenstown accommodation before checkout (~$3-5 NZD)
meals.lunch: Grab lunch on arrival in Wanaka - try Kai Whakapai Cafe & Bar or a bakery for a cheap pie (~$6-8 NZD)
meals.dinner: Ritual Cafe or Francesca's Italian Kitchen - affordable pasta dishes from ~$18-22 NZD

day_by_day.notes: The Crown Range road between Queenstown and Wanaka is scenic but can be steep and winding - if prone to motion sickness, take medication. Wanaka is significantly more affordable than Queenstown for accommodation and food. The town has a wonderful community feel and is less touristy. Book hostel in advance for November peak season.

day_by_day.morning: Hike the Diamond Lake and Rocky Mountain Loop Track near Wanaka (3-4 hours, free). Trailhead is 20 minutes drive from town (hitchhike or arrange a ride). The track climbs through farmland and rocky terrain to stunning views of Lake Wanaka, Mt Aspiring, and the surrounding ranges. Diamond Lake itself is a gorgeous turquoise gem.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Wanaka and visit the free Puzzling World attraction exterior (pay to enter if budget allows, ~$16 NZD - worth it for the optical illusions). Walk along the lake to Stuart Landsborough's Puzzling World area. Alternatively, visit the free Wanaka War Memorial and lakefront park.
day_by_day.evening: Cook dinner at the hostel kitchen using supermarket ingredients - a great way to meet fellow travellers. Alternatively, try Federal Diner for affordable, quality food. Enjoy a quiet evening in laid-back Wanaka.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hostel - muesli or toast (~$3-4 NZD)
meals.lunch: Pack trail snacks and sandwiches for the Diamond Lake hike (~$7-9 NZD)
meals.dinner: Self-catered hostel meal - stir-fry with rice and veggies (~$6-8 NZD) or Federal Diner (~$16-20 NZD)

day_by_day.notes: Diamond Lake track can be slippery after rain - wear proper hiking boots. The Rocky Mountain summit section involves some scrambling. Allow extra time if conditions are wet. Wanaka supermarkets (New World) are well-stocked - stock up on supplies here as Mount Cook has very limited shopping options and prices are much higher.

day_by_day.morning: Optional additional Wanaka activity: Hike the Roy's Peak Track (16km return, 5-6 hours, free) - one of the most iconic hikes in New Zealand with unbeatable views of Lake Wanaka and Mt Aspiring. Start very early (6:00am) to avoid crowds at the famous Instagram viewpoint and to beat the heat. This is a strenuous hike with 1,300m elevation gain.
day_by_day.afternoon: If doing Roy's Peak, you'll be descending in the afternoon. If skipping Roy's Peak, visit the Wanaka area's free Cardrona Valley scenic drive or explore the nearby Albert Town and Hawea Flat areas by bike or bus. Rest and prepare for the Mount Cook journey tomorrow.
day_by_day.evening: Last evening in Wanaka. Enjoy sunset at the lakefront one more time. Pack bags and prepare supplies for Mount Cook (stock up at New World supermarket as Mount Cook Village has very limited and expensive food options). Early night as tomorrow involves travel.

meals.breakfast: Very early self-catered breakfast at hostel if doing Roy's Peak (~$3-4 NZD)
meals.lunch: Packed trail food for Roy's Peak or cafe lunch in Wanaka if resting (~$8-12 NZD)
meals.dinner: Affordable pizza or burger in Wanaka town - try Amigos Mexican or Relishes Cafe (~$15-20 NZD)

day_by_day.notes: Roy's Peak is closed from October 1 to November 10 for lambing season - confirm it is open by November 23. If still closed, substitute with the Isthmus Peak Track on the other side of Lake Hawea (similar difficulty and views). Both tracks require good fitness. Carry plenty of water as there are no water sources on Roy's Peak.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day from Wanaka to Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park. Take the InterCity bus or arrange a shuttle (~$40-60 NZD) via Twizel. The journey takes approximately 3-4 hours with stunning scenery through the Mackenzie Basin, passing turquoise Lake Pukaki with Mt Cook visible in the distance - a jaw-dropping approach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Mount Cook Village (Aoraki/Mount Cook). Check in to budget accommodation at the YHA Mount Cook (~$35-45 NZD/night dorm) - the most affordable option in the village. Take the short Bowen Bush Walk (30 min loop, free) near the village to stretch legs after travel. Visit the Sir Edmund Hillary Alpine Centre (free exhibits outside).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the incredible stargazing from Mount Cook Village - it's one of the best dark sky locations in the Southern Hemisphere and the area is part of the Aoraki Mackenzie International Dark Sky Reserve. Watch the sunset paint the mountain pink (alpenglow). Cook dinner at the YHA kitchen.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at Wanaka hostel before departure (~$3-5 NZD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten on the bus or at a rest stop (~$7-9 NZD) - buy in Wanaka as options en route are expensive
meals.dinner: Self-catered at YHA kitchen - pasta or rice dish from supplies brought from Wanaka (~$6-8 NZD)

day_by_day.notes: CRITICAL: Stock up heavily on food in Wanaka or Twizel before arriving at Mount Cook. The only eating option in the village is the Old Mountaineers Cafe (expensive, ~$20-30 NZD per meal) or the Hermitage Hotel (very expensive). The YHA has a good kitchen. Bring 2-3 days of self-catering supplies. Book YHA in advance as it's the only budget option and fills quickly.

day_by_day.morning: HOOKER VALLEY TRACK: Start the iconic Hooker Valley Track early (8:00am). The 10km return trail through Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park crosses three swing bridges over glacial rivers with direct views of Aoraki/Mt Cook (3,724m - New Zealand's highest peak). Pass Mueller Glacier and Lake to reach Hooker Lake with floating icebergs. Free to hike.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the end of the Hooker Valley Track at Hooker Lake (allow 3-4 hours total return). The icebergs floating in the milky turquoise glacial lake with Mt Cook towering above is one of the most spectacular sights in New Zealand. Return along the same trail. Optional: extend the day with the short Kea Point Track (1.5 hours return, free) for views of Mueller Glacier.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the village. Visit the Sir Edmund Hillary Alpine Centre for the free exhibit about the first ascent of Everest and local mountaineering history. Stargaze again - on clear nights the Milky Way is extraordinary. Cook dinner at YHA. Early night for tomorrow's activities.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at YHA - oats or muesli before the hike (~$3-4 NZD)
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch eaten at Hooker Lake - sandwiches, energy bars, fruit (~$8-10 NZD)
meals.dinner: Self-catered at YHA kitchen - hearty meal to recover - rice and beans or pasta (~$6-8 NZD)

day_by_day.notes: The Hooker Valley Track is one of the most rewarding easy hikes in New Zealand - don't rush it. The track is well-formed and suitable for all fitness levels. Bring layers as the valley can be windy and cold even in November. The icebergs in Hooker Lake are a result of glacier retreat - a powerful reminder of climate change. Sandflies can be present near the lake - bring insect repellent.

day_by_day.morning: Hike the Sealy Tarns Track from the Kea Point carpark (3-4 hours return, free). This steep but rewarding trail climbs via metal ladders and steps to alpine tarns with incredible views of Aoraki/Mt Cook and the surrounding glaciers. More strenuous than the Hooker Valley but far fewer crowds. Elevation gain of approximately 700m.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the village by early afternoon. Begin travel back towards Christchurch direction. Take an afternoon bus or shuttle to Twizel (~$25-35 NZD, 1 hour) or Lake Tekapo (~$30-45 NZD, 1.5 hours). Check in to a budget hostel in Lake Tekapo (Tailor-Made Tekapo Hostel or YHA, ~$30-40 NZD/night).
day_by_day.evening: Visit the iconic Church of the Good Shepherd on the shores of Lake Tekapo at sunset (free, exterior). Walk along the turquoise Lake Tekapo shoreline. More incredible stargazing from Tekapo - visit the Mt John University Observatory for a stargazing tour (~$55 NZD) or simply stargaze for free from the lake edge.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at YHA Mount Cook - last use of supplies (~$3-5 NZD)
meals.lunch: Pack remaining supplies for trail lunch at Sealy Tarns (~$7-9 NZD)
meals.dinner: Kohan Japanese Restaurant in Lake Tekapo - affordable Japanese food from ~$18-22 NZD, or self-cater at hostel

day_by_day.notes: The Sealy Tarns metal ladder sections can be slippery when wet - take care. Lake Tekapo is another Dark Sky Reserve location and arguably has even better stargazing than Mount Cook village due to the reflections on the lake. The turquoise colour of Lake Tekapo comes from glacial flour (finely ground rock particles) suspended in the water. Stock up on groceries in Twizel if passing through as Tekapo's supermarket is small and expensive.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for sunrise over Lake Tekapo - the pink and orange light reflecting on the turquoise water with Mt Cook visible in the distance is magical. Walk to the Church of the Good Shepherd for golden hour photos (free). Hike the Mt John Summit Track (2-3 hours return, free) for 360-degree views of the Mackenzie Basin, multiple lakes, and the Southern Alps.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the InterCity bus or shuttle from Lake Tekapo to Christchurch (~$30-45 NZD, 3.5 hours). The journey crosses the Canterbury Plains with views of the Southern Alps. Arrive in Christchurch in the afternoon. If departing from Christchurch, head to the airport or central city. Explore the free Christchurch Botanic Gardens or the free Christchurch Art Gallery if time permits.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in New Zealand. Explore the Christchurch container mall (Re:START) and riverside Avon River precinct (free). Enjoy a farewell dinner at a local Christchurch restaurant. The city has a vibrant food scene with many affordable options.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at Lake Tekapo hostel - use up remaining supplies (~$3-5 NZD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the bus or stop at a cafe in Christchurch on arrival (~$10-14 NZD)
meals.dinner: Christchurch farewell dinner - try the Riverside Market food stalls for diverse affordable options from ~$12-18 NZD

day_by_day.notes: This is the final day of the 13-day itinerary. If your return flight departs from Christchurch, confirm flight times and allow at least 2.5 hours before departure for check-in. Christchurch Airport is 15-20 minutes from the city centre by bus (Metro Purple Line, ~$4 NZD) or taxi (~$35-45 NZD). If you have extra time in Christchurch, the free Transitional Cathedral and the Quake City museum ($20 NZD) are worthwhile stops to understand the 2011 earthquake recovery story.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Queenstown Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Queenstown Boutique Stay, freshen up, then take a leisurely stroll along Queenstown Bay waterfront and explore the town centre. Browse the shops on Beach Street and get oriented with the area.
day_by_day.evening: Ride the Skyline Gondola up Bob's Peak for panoramic views of Lake Wakatipu and The Remarkables at sunset — a perfect gentle introduction to Queenstown.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy snacks or a meal on the flight
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at Fergbaker bakery near the town centre after check-in — great pies and sandwiches at a reasonable price
meals.dinner: Dinner at Rata Restaurant on Ballarat Street — locally sourced New Zealand cuisine in a relaxed mid-range setting

day_by_day.notes: Flight arrives at 13:00. Allow at least 45 minutes for baggage and transport to the hotel. Keep Day 1 light to recover from travel. Book Skyline Gondola tickets online in advance to save time.

day_by_day.morning: Kawarau Bridge Bungy Jump — head to the world's first commercial bungy site, 43 meters above the Kawarau River. Book the early morning slot for smaller crowds. Watch others jump before taking the plunge yourself.
day_by_day.afternoon: Recovery and exploration: drive or take a short bus to Arrowtown, a charming historic gold-mining village 20 minutes from Queenstown. Walk the Arrow River trail and browse the heritage museum.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown. Wander the lively Queenstown waterfront and enjoy the vibrant atmosphere along the lakefront promenade.

meals.breakfast: Eat before the bungy — try Vudu Cafe & Larder on Rees Street for eggs, coffee and fresh pastries
meals.lunch: Lunch in Arrowtown at The Fork and Tap — great burgers and local craft beers in a relaxed pub setting
meals.dinner: Dinner at Winnies Gourmet Pizza Bar in Queenstown town centre — lively atmosphere, generous portions, mid-range pricing

day_by_day.notes: Book the Kawarau Bridge Bungy with AJ Hackett well in advance online. Arrive at least 30 minutes early for registration and briefing. Wear comfortable clothes you don't mind getting wet. Arrowtown is approximately 20 km from Queenstown.

day_by_day.morning: Routeburn Track Day Hike — depart early (7:00 AM) for the Routeburn Shelter trailhead, approximately 1 hour from Queenstown. Hike through ancient beech forest with stunning views of the Humboldt Mountains and alpine meadows.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along the Routeburn Track to Routeburn Flats and back, enjoying the river valleys and snow-capped peaks. Total hike is approximately 16–18 km return from the shelter.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown in the late afternoon. Rest tired legs, shower, and enjoy a relaxed evening in town.

meals.breakfast: Pack a takeaway breakfast from Vudu Cafe the night before — muffins, fruit and coffee in a thermos
meals.lunch: Pack a trail lunch: sandwiches, trail mix, and fruit from a Queenstown supermarket (New World on Gorge Road is convenient)
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Bunker restaurant in Queenstown — cosy atmosphere, excellent New Zealand lamb and beef dishes, mid-range prices

day_by_day.notes: Start early to maximise daylight and avoid afternoon weather changes. Wear sturdy hiking boots and bring waterproof layers — weather in the Routeburn can change rapidly. Carry at least 2 litres of water per person. No shuttle booking needed for day hikers starting from the shelter.

day_by_day.morning: Nevis Bungy Jump — New Zealand's highest bungy at 134 meters, suspended in a gondola above the Nevis River. A thrilling and unforgettable experience. Transfer departs from AJ Hackett base in Queenstown town centre.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the adrenaline rush, relax with a scenic jet boat ride on the Shotover River or simply unwind at the hotel and review your Nevis jump video and photos.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory dinner in Queenstown to mark the achievement of completing both iconic AJ Hackett bungy experiences.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the hotel or grab something small — avoid eating too heavily before the jump
meals.lunch: Post-jump treat at Fergburger, Queenstown's legendary burger institution — try the 'Son of a Bun' or 'Bun Laden'
meals.dinner: Dinner at Amisfield Bistro & Cellar (20 minutes from Queenstown near Lake Hayes) — award-winning local wine and seasonal dishes; mid-to-upper mid-range

day_by_day.notes: The Nevis Bungy requires a 4WD transfer from Queenstown — this is included in the AJ Hackett package. Minimum weight is 45 kg, maximum 127 kg. Book well in advance. The experience including transfer takes approximately 3–4 hours total.

day_by_day.morning: Active recovery day — take a gentle hike on the Queenstown Hill Walkway (Te Tapu-nui). The 2–3 hour return trail offers sweeping views over Lake Wakatipu and The Remarkables without being too strenuous.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Queenstown Gardens — stroll through the rose garden, frisbee golf course and lakeside paths. Rent a kayak or paddleboard on Lake Wakatipu for a relaxing paddle.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the vibrant Queenstown night scene along the waterfront. Visit a local wine bar to sample Central Otago Pinot Noir.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Bespoke Kitchen on Isle Street — excellent smoothie bowls, eggs and plant-based options
meals.lunch: Lakeside lunch at Hawthorne Coffee House near the Queenstown Gardens — great sandwiches and coffee with garden views
meals.dinner: Dinner at Botswana Butchery on Marine Parade — lakeside views, premium New Zealand beef and lamb, mid-to-upper mid-range

day_by_day.notes: This is a planned rest and recovery day after two major bungy jumps. Keep activities light. The Queenstown Hill Walkway is well-signposted and suitable for all fitness levels. Paddleboard rentals are available from operators along the lakefront.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Wanaka (approximately 1 hour from Queenstown via the Crown Range Road — the highest sealed road in New Zealand). Stop at the Crown Range lookout for spectacular views over the Cardrona Valley.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Wanaka town and hike the Rob Roy Glacier Track (approximately 10 km return, 4 hours) in the Mount Aspiring National Park — stunning glacier views, swing bridges and waterfalls. Alternatively, hike Mount Iron for panoramic Wanaka views (shorter, 1.5 hours).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Wanaka's relaxed lakeside village atmosphere. Stroll along the famous Wanaka Tree on the lake edge at sunset.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast in Queenstown before departing — try Vudu Cafe again or pick up supplies from New World supermarket
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch for the Rob Roy hike, or grab a bite at Wanaka's Francesca's Italian Kitchen after the hike
meals.dinner: Dinner at Kika on Helwick Street in Wanaka — modern New Zealand sharing plates with local produce; excellent mid-range option

day_by_day.notes: The Crown Range Road is spectacular but can be narrow and winding — drive carefully. For Rob Roy Glacier Track, a 4WD vehicle is recommended for the last section of road to the Raspberry Creek car park. Check road conditions before departure. Return to Queenstown for the night.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park (approximately 3.5 hours from Queenstown via State Highway 8 through the Mackenzie Basin). Enjoy the spectacular drive past Lake Pukaki with its vivid turquoise glacial waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hooker Valley Track to Mueller Glacier — one of New Zealand's most iconic and accessible alpine hikes. The 10 km return track crosses three swing bridges and ends at a glacial lake with dramatic views of Aoraki/Mount Cook (3,724 m).
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Mount Cook Village area. Visit the Sir Edmund Hillary Alpine Centre at The Hermitage for an inspiring film and exhibition about New Zealand's greatest mountaineer.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast in Queenstown before the long drive — fuel up well for the day ahead
meals.lunch: Pack a hearty trail lunch for the Hooker Valley Track — sandwiches, snacks and plenty of water
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Old Mountaineers' Café and Bar in Mount Cook Village — casual, mid-range, excellent burgers and local craft beers with views of the mountains

day_by_day.notes: This is a long driving day — depart by 7:30 AM. The stop at Lake Pukaki is unmissable; allow 20 minutes. The Hooker Valley Track is well-formed and suitable for most fitness levels but can be windy. Overnight stay in Mount Cook Village is recommended — book accommodation separately if extending, or return to Queenstown (4+ hours drive back, not recommended).

day_by_day.morning: Morning walk to Kea Point Track (2 hours return) for close-up views of the Mueller Glacier and terminal lake — a quieter alternative to the Hooker Valley Track with equally stunning scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive back toward Queenstown via the Mackenzie Basin. Stop at Lake Tekapo for a visit to the Church of the Good Shepherd and a walk around the lake edge. The Tekapo Springs is a great option for a warm soak after days of hiking.
day_by_day.evening: Continue drive back to Queenstown. Arrive by early evening and enjoy a relaxed night in town.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at The Old Mountaineers' Café in Mount Cook Village before the morning hike
meals.lunch: Lunch at Kohan Japanese Restaurant in Lake Tekapo — unexpectedly excellent Japanese cuisine with lake views; great mid-range option
meals.dinner: Casual dinner back in Queenstown at Pub on Wharf — relaxed waterfront pub with good food and local beers

day_by_day.notes: Tekapo Springs entry fee is approximately NZD $25–35 per person — worth it after several days of hiking. The Church of the Good Shepherd is a short walk from the main road and is free to visit. Lake Tekapo is approximately 2.5 hours from Mount Cook and 2.5 hours from Queenstown.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Te Anau (approximately 2 hours from Queenstown via State Highway 6). Te Anau is the gateway to Fiordland National Park. Check in to accommodation and walk the Te Anau lakefront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kepler Track Day Hike — take the short boat shuttle across Lake Te Anau and hike a section of the Kepler Track through ancient beech forest to the Brod Bay picnic area and back (approximately 3–4 hours, easy to moderate).
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Te Anau Glowworm Caves — a magical 2-hour guided tour by boat into limestone caves filled with thousands of glowworms, operated by Real Journeys.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast in Queenstown before departing — pick up supplies from New World for the drive
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at Brod Bay on the Kepler Track — picnic tables available with lake views
meals.dinner: Dinner at Redcliff Restaurant in Te Anau — cosy heritage cottage setting, excellent New Zealand venison and lamb, mid-range pricing

day_by_day.notes: Book the Te Anau Glowworm Caves tour with Real Journeys well in advance — evening tours are popular. The boat shuttle for the Kepler Track departs from the Te Anau lakefront. Overnight in Te Anau — book a mid-range guesthouse or motel separately for this night.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Te Anau early for Milford Sound (approximately 2 hours via the spectacular Milford Road — one of the world's great scenic drives). Stop at Mirror Lakes, The Chasm and Homer Tunnel along the way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Milford Sound Cruise — a 2-hour scenic cruise through the fiord with views of Mitre Peak, Stirling Falls and Bowen Falls. Keep an eye out for seals, dolphins and penguins. Afternoon cruises are often less crowded.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Te Anau (2 hours) or return to Queenstown (approximately 4 hours). Enjoy a quiet evening recovering from a spectacular day.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast in Te Anau before the drive — grab supplies from the Four Square supermarket
meals.lunch: Café lunch at the Milford Sound Lodge Café or pack your own — options at Milford Sound are limited and pricey, so packing is recommended
meals.dinner: If returning to Te Anau: dinner at Miles Better Pies & Cafe — casual and affordable. If returning to Queenstown: dinner at The Bunker

day_by_day.notes: Depart Te Anau no later than 7:30 AM. The Milford Road can be closed due to avalanche risk in bad weather — check conditions the night before at the NZTA website. Book the Milford Sound cruise in advance with Real Journeys or Jucy Cruise. The drive alone is worth the trip — allow extra time for stops.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Queenstown if not already back. Take a relaxed morning to explore the Queenstown Farmer's Market (held Saturday mornings at the Earnslaw Park) — browse local produce, artisan food and crafts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the Ben Lomond Track to the saddle (approximately 3–4 hours return to the saddle, or 5–6 hours return to the summit at 1,748 m for the more ambitious). Access via the Skyline Gondola for a head start. Incredible 360-degree views over Queenstown and Lake Wakatipu.
day_by_day.evening: Final Queenstown evening — enjoy a sunset drink on the Skyline deck if you rode the gondola, then head into town.

meals.breakfast: Sample food from the Queenstown Farmer's Market — fresh pastries, local cheeses and seasonal produce
meals.lunch: Pack trail snacks and lunch for the Ben Lomond hike
meals.dinner: Dinner at Fishbone Bar & Grill on Beach Street — excellent fresh New Zealand seafood, mid-range pricing

day_by_day.notes: The Queenstown Farmer's Market runs every Saturday morning. Ben Lomond is a significant hike — the summit attempt adds considerable difficulty and should only be attempted in good weather with proper gear. Check the weather forecast the evening before. The gondola saves approximately 400 m of elevation gain.

day_by_day.morning: Scenic drive along the shores of Lake Wakatipu to Glenorchy (approximately 45 minutes from Queenstown) — one of the most beautiful drives in New Zealand. Glenorchy was used as a filming location for Lord of the Rings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the Paradise area near Glenorchy — explore the flat river valley walks through the Dart River flats and beech forest (2–3 hours, easy). The landscape is truly otherworldly. Alternatively, join a guided Dart River Jet Safari.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown for a final evening. Treat yourself to a farewell dinner and pick up souvenirs from the town centre shops.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Glenorchy Café on arrival — excellent coffee, eggs and baked goods in a charming setting
meals.lunch: Packed lunch in the Paradise Valley — picnic by the Dart River
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Rata Restaurant — celebrate the end of an incredible trip with New Zealand's finest seasonal cuisine

day_by_day.notes: The road to Glenorchy is sealed and suitable for all vehicles. The road beyond Glenorchy toward Paradise becomes gravel — a standard 2WD car can usually manage in dry conditions but check locally. The Glenorchy area is incredibly photogenic — bring your camera. Allow time to visit the Glenorchy lagoon and jetty.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Queenstown — depending on flight time, enjoy a leisurely breakfast and a last walk along the Queenstown waterfront or through the Queenstown Gardens. Pack and check out of the Queenstown Boutique Stay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Queenstown Airport for departure. Allow at least 2 hours before flight for check-in and security. Grab any last-minute New Zealand souvenirs at the airport — Whittaker's chocolate, Manuka honey and Merino wool products are great options.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Queenstown Airport. Reflect on an incredible 13-day South Island adventure featuring world-class hiking, New Zealand's most iconic bungy jumps, fiords, glaciers and alpine landscapes.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at a Queenstown favourite — Vudu Cafe & Larder for a proper send-off meal
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport or grab a pie from Fergbaker for the road
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or at transit airport

day_by_day.notes: Check your flight departure time carefully and plan your morning accordingly. Queenstown Airport is only 10 minutes from the town centre. Return any rental car with a full tank of fuel to avoid surcharges. Keep a layer accessible in carry-on luggage as temperatures can change significantly during transit.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium New Zealand South Island Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Tongariro Alpine Crossing
experiences.description: One of New Zealand's most iconic day hikes, crossing volcanic terrain with stunning views of emerald lakes and craters. Book an early shuttle from Queenstown or Wanaka to maximize daylight hours on the trail. Stay in Taupo or National Park Village the night before to avoid wasting time on Day 1 with a late arrival.
experiences.location: Tongariro National Park, Central North Island

experiences.name: Nevis Bungy Jump
experiences.description: New Zealand's highest bungy jump at 134 meters, operated by AJ Hackett in a gondola suspended above the Nevis River. A bucket-list adrenaline experience near Queenstown. Book in advance to secure your preferred time slot and combine with nearby accommodation in Queenstown central to avoid long transfers.

experiences.name: Routeburn Track Day Hike
experiences.description: A world-class multi-day track accessible as a rewarding day hike from the Routeburn Shelter trailhead. Offers dramatic alpine scenery, beech forests, and mountain views. Stay in Glenorchy village (45 min from Queenstown) the night before to get an early start and make the most of the trail without rushing.

experiences.name: Kawarau Bridge Bungy
experiences.description: The world's first commercial bungy jump site at 43 meters above the Kawarau River, operated by AJ Hackett. A historic and thrilling experience with a scenic river backdrop. Located just 23 km from Queenstown central, making it easy to combine with central accommodation and other Queenstown activities on the same day.

experiences.name: Hooker Valley Track to Mueller Glacier
experiences.description: A relatively easy but breathtaking 10 km return hike through Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park, crossing swing bridges with direct views of New Zealand's highest peak and glacial lakes. Stay in Mount Cook Village (within the park) to eliminate long morning drives and enjoy the trail at golden hour with fewer crowds.
experiences.location: Mount Cook Village, Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Queenstown Airport at 13:00. Private luxury transfer to Queenstown Boutique Stay. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll along the Queenstown waterfront promenade overlooking Lake Wakatipu and The Remarkables mountain range.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset gondola ride up Bob's Peak for panoramic views of Queenstown. Enjoy a welcome cocktail at the summit bar before descending for a relaxed first dinner in town.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport lounge
meals.lunch: Light arrival bite at Queenstown Airport's premium lounge or a quick stop at Vudu Cafe & Larder for artisan sandwiches and coffee
meals.dinner: Rata Restaurant by Chef Josh Emett — celebrated New Zealand cuisine with locally sourced Canterbury lamb, Central Otago pinot noir pairings, in a warm heritage building setting

day_by_day.notes: Request early check-in with the hotel in advance. Arrange private airport transfer ahead of time. Keep Day 1 relaxed to recover from long-haul travel.

day_by_day.morning: Kawarau Bridge Bungy Jump — the world's first commercial bungy site at 43 meters above the Kawarau River, operated by AJ Hackett. Book the first session of the day for smaller crowds. Watch other jumpers from the glass viewing platform if accompanying non-jumpers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Scenic drive to Arrowtown, a charming gold-rush era village 20 minutes from Queenstown. Explore the historic Chinese Settlement, boutique galleries, and the Arrow River walking trail through autumn gold poplars (stunning in November).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown for a premium dining experience with lake views.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast at Queenstown Boutique Stay — request a full New Zealand spread with local cheeses, manuka honey, and fresh fruit
meals.lunch: The Chop Shop Food Merchants in Arrowtown — craft burgers and local craft beers in a relaxed gold-rush setting
meals.dinner: Amisfield Winery & Bistro — estate-grown Central Otago pinot noir paired with a seasonal tasting menu in a stunning vineyard setting just outside Queenstown

day_by_day.notes: Book the Kawarau Bridge Bungy in advance through AJ Hackett's website. Arrive 30 minutes early for briefing and gear fitting. Wear comfortable clothing and closed-toe shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Routeburn Track Day Hike — depart early from Queenstown (approx. 1.5-hour drive to the Routeburn Shelter trailhead). Hike through ancient beech forests, past cascading waterfalls, and alpine meadows with dramatic views of the Humboldt Mountains. A world-class trail on a world-class day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue hiking to Routeburn Falls Hut (approximately 4 hours return from the shelter) for sweeping valley views, then begin the return descent through lush Fiordland forest.
day_by_day.evening: Return drive to Queenstown. Relax with a soak in the hotel's facilities before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast or a pre-packed luxury picnic hamper arranged by the hotel for the trail
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed lunch on the trail — request the hotel prepare a premium hamper with charcuterie, local cheeses, fruit, and thermos of coffee
meals.dinner: Botswana Butchery Queenstown — premium cuts of New Zealand grass-fed beef and South Island salmon, with an extensive Central Otago wine list, lakefront views

day_by_day.notes: Hire a private guide or arrange a guided day hike with Routeburn Guided Walks for a premium experience. Wear layered hiking gear — alpine conditions can change rapidly even in November. Bring trekking poles, sunscreen, and plenty of water.

day_by_day.morning: Nevis Bungy Jump — New Zealand's highest bungy at 134 meters, suspended in a gondola above the Nevis River gorge. A truly world-class adrenaline experience. Transfer departs from AJ Hackett's Queenstown base on Shotover Street.
day_by_day.afternoon: Post-bungy recovery and celebration. Visit the Queenstown Gardens for a peaceful lakeside walk, or enjoy a private e-bike tour along the Queenstown Trail along the shores of Lake Wakatipu.
day_by_day.evening: Luxury dinner cruise on Lake Wakatipu aboard the historic TSS Earnslaw steamship, with a private dinner option at Walter Peak High Country Farm.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — fuel up well before the jump with protein-rich options
meals.lunch: Pub lunch at Sherwood Queenstown — farm-to-table casual dining with craft cocktails in a relaxed garden setting
meals.dinner: Walter Peak Colonel's Homestead Restaurant — gourmet buffet dinner with live entertainment, accessed by the iconic TSS Earnslaw steamship across Lake Wakatipu. Book the premium private dining option.

day_by_day.notes: The Nevis Bungy requires a 45-minute 4WD transfer from Queenstown — factor this into your morning schedule. Weight and health restrictions apply; check AJ Hackett's requirements in advance. The TSS Earnslaw dinner cruise must be booked well ahead of time.

day_by_day.morning: Luxury heli-hiking experience — fly by private helicopter from Queenstown to a remote alpine landing zone on the Richardson Mountains or Cecil Peak. Hike with a private guide through pristine high-country terrain inaccessible by foot, with jaw-dropping 360-degree views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Helicopter return to Queenstown. Afternoon at leisure — browse the premium boutiques on Beach Street, visit the Kiwi Birdlife Park, or indulge in a spa treatment at the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Queenstown's finest fine dining experience for a mid-trip celebration night.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: In-flight picnic lunch provided by helicopter operator on the mountain, or post-flight lunch at Fergburger (iconic Queenstown institution — lines worth it)
meals.dinner: The Bunker Restaurant — Queenstown's most intimate and acclaimed fine dining venue, hidden down a cobblestone lane. Exceptional tasting menu with wine pairings.

day_by_day.notes: Book heli-hiking through Glacier Southern Lakes Helicopters or Over The Top Helicopters. Weather-dependent activity — have a backup plan. The Bunker requires reservations well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury drive to Milford Sound (approx. 4 hours from Queenstown via Te Anau). Stop at Mirror Lakes and the Avenue of the Disappearing Mountain along the Milford Road for photography.
day_by_day.afternoon: Premium small-group or private Milford Sound cruise — sail past Mitre Peak, Stirling Falls, and Lady Bowen Falls. Watch for dolphins, seals, and penguins. Opt for a kayaking add-on for an intimate water-level experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return drive toward Te Anau. Overnight stay in Te Anau at a premium lodge to break the journey.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Queenstown before departure
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic lunch on the Milford Sound cruise deck, or the premium catered lunch option aboard the vessel
meals.dinner: Fiordland Lodge Restaurant in Te Anau — stunning fiordland views, locally sourced venison and salmon, exceptional wine list

day_by_day.notes: Book the Real Journeys Milford Sound Nature Cruise or Cruise Milford's premium vessel for the best experience. Depart Queenstown no later than 7:30 AM to make the cruise. Sandflies are ferocious at Milford — bring strong insect repellent.

day_by_day.morning: Morning walk around the Te Anau glowworm caves — a magical underground boat journey through limestone caves lit by thousands of glowworms (Arachnocampa luminosa). Book through Real Journeys.
day_by_day.afternoon: Scenic drive back toward Queenstown, stopping at Lake Marian for a short but rewarding hike (2.5 hours return) through Fiordland forest to a stunning alpine lake surrounded by towering peaks.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown Boutique Stay. Relaxed evening with room service or a quiet dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Fiordland Lodge or a Te Anau lakefront café
meals.lunch: Redcliff Café in Te Anau — warm, character-filled restaurant with excellent venison pie and local craft beer before the drive back
meals.dinner: Kappa Japanese Restaurant Queenstown — premium omakase-style Japanese dining with fresh South Island seafood, a refined change of pace

day_by_day.notes: Te Anau Glowworm Caves tours run at set times — book the morning session in advance. Lake Marian trail can be muddy; waterproof hiking boots recommended. The drive from Te Anau back to Queenstown is approximately 2 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury scenic flight from Queenstown over Aoraki/Mount Cook, the Southern Alps, and the Franz Josef and Fox Glaciers. A breathtaking aerial perspective of New Zealand's most dramatic landscapes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or fly to Mount Cook Village (approximately 4 hours by road or 45 minutes by scenic flight). Check in at The Hermitage Hotel — New Zealand's most iconic mountain lodge with direct views of Aoraki/Mount Cook.
day_by_day.evening: Stargazing experience in the Aoraki Mackenzie International Dark Sky Reserve — one of the world's largest dark sky reserves. Guided telescope session with an astronomer.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Queenstown
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet hamper for the journey or stop at a Cromwell or Twizel café en route
meals.dinner: The Hermitage's Panorama Restaurant — fine dining with floor-to-ceiling windows framing Aoraki/Mount Cook at dusk, featuring Canterbury lamb and Central Otago wines

day_by_day.notes: Book the scenic flight with Glacier Southern Lakes Helicopters or Air Safaris. The Hermitage Hotel is the premium option at Mount Cook — book well in advance for rooms with mountain views. Stargazing tours run through Earth & Sky Ltd — book ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Hooker Valley Track to Mueller Glacier — a breathtaking 10 km return hike through Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park, crossing swing bridges over glacial rivers with direct views of the Mueller Glacier and the summit of Aoraki/Mount Cook. One of the most spectacular easy hikes in New Zealand.
day_by_day.afternoon: Sealy Tarns Track — a more challenging extension hike (approximately 3 hours return) climbing above the Hooker Valley to alpine tarns with panoramic views of the Main Divide. Or opt for a glacier kayaking experience on the Tasman Glacier terminal lake.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at The Hermitage. Soak in the alpine atmosphere and enjoy the hotel's premium facilities.

meals.breakfast: The Hermitage breakfast — fuel up for a big hiking day
meals.lunch: Old Mountaineers' Café at Mount Cook Village — legendary café with hearty soups, pies, and stunning mountain views from the deck
meals.dinner: The Hermitage's Alpine Restaurant — more casual dining option with hearty New Zealand comfort food and local craft beers after a big hiking day

day_by_day.notes: Start the Hooker Valley Track early (by 8:00 AM) to avoid midday crowds and enjoy the best light on the glacier. Glacier kayaking is available through Glacier Explorers — a truly unique experience. Weather can change rapidly at altitude.

day_by_day.morning: Tasman Glacier Boat Tour — explore the terminal lake of New Zealand's largest glacier, weaving through icebergs calved from the glacier face. A dramatic and humbling experience with a private guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Scenic drive from Mount Cook toward Wanaka (approximately 3 hours via the Lindis Pass). Stop at Lake Pukaki's brilliant turquoise shores for photography, and at Twizel for a coffee break.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Wanaka. Check in at a premium Wanaka lakeside lodge. Sunset walk along the Wanaka lakefront.

meals.breakfast: The Hermitage breakfast before checkout
meals.lunch: Stop at Pukaki Salmon Farm Shop near Lake Pukaki — fresh-smoked salmon, salmon pâté, and local produce for a scenic lakeside picnic
meals.dinner: Francesca's Italian Kitchen in Wanaka — beloved fine Italian dining with handmade pasta, wood-fired dishes, and an exceptional Italian and New Zealand wine list

day_by_day.notes: Glacier Explorers runs the Tasman Glacier boat tour — book in advance as it is weather-dependent. The drive from Mount Cook to Wanaka via Lindis Pass is one of New Zealand's most scenic road journeys. Recommend staying at Edgewater Resort or Wanaka Springs Lodge.

day_by_day.morning: Roys Peak Track — Wanaka's most iconic hike, a challenging 16 km return with 1,279 m elevation gain to a summit with sweeping views of Lake Wanaka, Mount Aspiring, and the Southern Alps. Start at dawn for the best light and to beat the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend Roys Peak and recover with a lakeside lunch. Afternoon at leisure — paddleboard or kayak on Lake Wanaka, or visit the Puzzling World attraction for a fun interlude.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a Wanaka lakefront bar followed by a premium dinner.

meals.breakfast: Pre-dawn packed breakfast from the hotel before the hike
meals.lunch: Ritual Café Wanaka — excellent post-hike brunch with smashed avocado, eggs benedict, and specialty coffee on the lakefront
meals.dinner: Bistro Gentil Wanaka — sophisticated fine dining in a garden setting, with an emphasis on French-New Zealand fusion and an outstanding wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: Roys Peak is closed during lambing season (October 1 – November 10) — by November 25 it should be open, but confirm with the Department of Conservation before going. Start no later than 6:00 AM for sunrise views at the summit. Bring 2+ liters of water.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided hike in the Mount Aspiring National Park — explore the Rob Roy Glacier Track (10 km return, 3–4 hours) through ancient beech forest to a dramatic hanging glacier and waterfall amphitheatre. One of New Zealand's finest half-day hikes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Wanaka. Visit the Rippon Vineyard on the shores of Lake Wanaka for a premium wine tasting of their certified biodynamic pinot noir and riesling, with stunning lake-and-mountain views.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in the South Island. Scenic drive back to Queenstown (approximately 1 hour) and check back in to Queenstown Boutique Stay for the last night.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Wanaka
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch at Rob Roy Glacier — arrange a premium hamper from the Wanaka hotel
meals.dinner: Rata Restaurant Queenstown — return to where the trip began for a celebratory final dinner, indulging in the full tasting menu with wine pairings to mark the end of an extraordinary journey

day_by_day.notes: The Rob Roy Glacier Track requires a 45-minute drive from Wanaka on a gravel road — a 4WD vehicle is recommended. Rippon Vineyard tastings are by appointment only — book in advance. Allow time for the Wanaka to Queenstown drive before dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Queenstown. Last lakefront walk along the Queenstown Bay waterfront. Browse the Queenstown Saturday Artisan Market for premium New Zealand souvenirs — local honey, merino wool products, artisan crafts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time — optional final activity: scenic jet boat ride on the Shotover River (Shotover Jet) for a last adrenaline hit, or a relaxed wine tasting at Gibbston Valley Winery in the Kawarau Gorge.
day_by_day.evening: Private luxury transfer to Queenstown Airport. Farewell to the South Island.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast at Queenstown Boutique Stay — take your time and savour it
meals.lunch: Eichardt's Private Hotel Bar — premium bar snacks and New Zealand craft beer or wine in Queenstown's most elegant historic hotel
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or an early dinner at Queenstown's waterfront before transfer if flight permits

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Check out time is typically 11:00 AM — arrange late checkout with the hotel if your flight is in the evening. Pack merino wool layers purchased during the trip for the journey home. Allow extra time at Queenstown Airport as it can be busy during peak season.

query: New Zealand South Island, $4000, hiking and bungee jumping, November 2026
